stem: Your colleague's Terraform apply against LocalStack hangs for 30 seconds and then fails with "NoCredentialProviders: no valid providers in chain". Which provider argument, if added and set to `true`, would prevent that specific hang?
objective: Explain the purpose of each LocalStack-specific provider argument (skip_credentials_validation, skip_metadata_api_check, endpoints block)

stem: A teammate configures the AWS provider for LocalStack but leaves out the `endpoints` block entirely. What happens when they run `terraform apply` on an `aws_s3_bucket` resource?
options: Terraform skips the S3 call and applies a default empty bucket.
Terraform creates the bucket in LocalStack because LocalStack intercepts all outbound traffic on port 443.
Terraform contacts the real AWS S3 API at s3.amazonaws.com, which rejects the mock credentials.
Terraform raises a schema validation error before making any API call.
objective: Explain the purpose of each LocalStack-specific provider argument (skip_credentials_validation, skip_metadata_api_check, endpoints block)

stem: You write an AWS provider block for LocalStack with mock credentials, both skip flags set to `true`, and an `endpoints` block. When you run `terraform validate`, Terraform reports the configuration is valid. What does this confirm?
options: LocalStack is running and accepted a test connection from the provider.
The endpoints block URLs are reachable from your machine.
The provider block's HCL syntax and argument names are recognised by the AWS provider schema.
The mock credentials will be accepted by LocalStack when you run terraform apply.
objective: Write an AWS provider block that uses mock credentials, sets skip flags, and points service endpoints at LocalStack so no real AWS API calls are made
